Give exceptions a place, an owner and a next step.

Exception Studio turns a failed or questionable record into a visible workflow. An analyst can investigate and repair it; a separate approver role controls the next delivery step. Durable jobs and an audit trail keep the state understandable when an attempt fails.

The Team Edition connects a React and TypeScript interface to a Node.js API and SQLite store. I built bounded retry behaviour, schema repair, lease fencing, reasoned replay and duplicate-safe sandbox delivery into the flow.

  • React & TypeScript
  • Node.js API
  • SQLite persistence
  • Durable jobs
  • Role checks
  • Failure recovery

The demo’s analyst and approver roles demonstrate access separation in code. They do not establish enterprise identity integration or an independent human approval process.

110 tests, with the layers named.

The test total is a sum of defined suites, rather than a claim about every possible application behaviour.

81 tests
Domain, persistence, HTTP and transport behaviour, including the rules and state transitions behind the workflow.
29 tests
UI behaviour in a simulated DOM. These checks exercise interface states and interactions; they are distinct from full-browser end-to-end tests.
Count scope
110 automated tests in the recorded Team Edition verification. The public repository contains the code and test definitions.

What the count establishes

These checks provide repeatable evidence for the covered behaviour. A test total alone does not establish complete security, accessibility, production reliability or performance under load.

Check the deployed recovery path.

On 28 October 2026, I verified seven recovery scenarios against the hosted application using fictional workspaces and records. The recorded outcomes show seven delivered jobs and seven destination writes, including one recognised duplicate.

That destination check matters: an apparently successful retry is not enough if the destination receives the same intended result twice. The verification record connects each scenario to the resulting job and destination state.

Environment
The hosted public demo with fictional data and a sandbox destination.
Recorded scope
Seven selected recovery scenarios, with seven delivered jobs, seven destination writes and one recognised duplicate.
Interpretation
Observed results for these cases. They are not a production success-rate estimate or a guarantee of exactly-once effects in every external system.

Try it, read the decisions and check the record.

The live demonstration shows the workflow. The repository makes the implementation inspectable, and the verification record captures the hosted checks separately from the automated suite.
